criteria.statement: Map validation accepts a `design-map.json` whose boards carry `"core": true` or `"core": false`, with no more than 8 Core boards, all of kind `to-be` or `as-is`
criteria.cites: After s1: "a board may carry `"core": true|false`; at most 8 are Core, and only `to-be` and `as-is` boards may be"
criteria.evidence: Output of the map validator run on a fixture map mixing `core: true` and `core: false` boards (8 Core, all to-be/as-is), showing it passes with exit code 0; saved under `evidence/FS-1/`

criteria.statement: Map validation rejects a `design-map.json` that marks more than 8 boards Core, and says the limit was exceeded
criteria.evidence: Output of the map validator run on a fixture map with 9 `to-be`/`as-is` boards marked `core: true`: non-zero exit (or an error result) naming the Core-board limit; saved under `evidence/FS-2/`

criteria.statement: Map validation rejects `"core": true` on a board that is neither `to-be` nor `as-is` (for example a `part` board or a `flow` board)
criteria.cites: After s1: "only `to-be` and `as-is` boards may be"
criteria.evidence: Validator output on two fixture maps, one with `core: true` on a `part` board and one on a `flow` board, each rejected with an error naming the board; saved under `evidence/FS-3/`

criteria.statement: A legacy map, one in which no board carries a `core` key, is read with every screen board treated as Core: the comparison-row generator classes the default-state frame of every screen board `core`
criteria.cites: After s2: "A map with no `core` key anywhere is a legacy map, and every screen board in it reads as Core"
criteria.evidence: Comparison-row generator output on a fixture map with no `core` key anywhere, showing one `core` row per screen board's default-state frame; saved under `evidence/FS-4/`

criteria.statement: The design-comparison rows are produced by a CLI from the map, not written by a model, and the same map always yields the same rows
criteria.cites: After s3: "A deterministic CLI generates the comparison rows from the map"; Today s2: "with no code generating them"
criteria.evidence: The CLI run twice on one fixture map, both outputs saved under `evidence/FS-5/`, plus a `diff` of the two showing no difference

criteria.statement: Every generated comparison row carries a class: `core` for the default-state frame of a Core board, and `evidence-only` for every other frame, including every frame of a non-Core board and a Core board's non-default states and second viewport
criteria.cites: After s3: "each carrying a class: `core` for the default-state frame of a Core board, `evidence-only` for every other frame"; Today s3 names the other frames: "an error state, a loading state, a second viewport"
criteria.evidence: CLI output on a fixture map holding a Core board with a default state plus an error state, a loading state and a second viewport, and one non-Core board: exactly one `core` row (the Core board's default state), every other row `evidence-only`; saved under `evidence/FS-6/`

criteria.statement: A 12-board fixture design with 8 Core boards yields exactly 8 must-pass (`core`) and 4 `evidence-only` design-comparison criteria
criteria.cites: Acceptance: "a 12-board fixture design yields 8 must-pass and 4 evidence-only criteria"
criteria.evidence: CLI output on the 12-board fixture, with a count of rows per class (8 `core`, 4 `evidence-only`); saved under `evidence/FS-7/`

criteria.statement: The success definition written for a design-comparison check records each row's class, so a reader of the definition file can tell which rows are `core` and which are `evidence-only`
criteria.cites: After s4: "The success definition records the class per row"
criteria.evidence: A success-definition file produced from the 12-board fixture, with its design-comparison rows showing the class of each row; saved under `evidence/FS-8/`

criteria.statement: The verification loop gets the set of evidence-only criterion ids by reading the success-definition file in code, not from a model's reading
criteria.cites: After s4: "the verification loop reads the evidence-only ids from the definition file in code"
criteria.evidence: Output of the loop's library function (or a unit test exercising it) that, given a fixture definition file, returns exactly the ids whose rows are classed `evidence-only`; saved under `evidence/FS-9/`

criteria.statement: An `evidence-only` criterion ruled `not_met` is not an open gap: it is not handed to the Debug stage and does not make the loop iterate again
criteria.cites: After s4: "never fails a run on one"
criteria.evidence: Output of the loop's control-flow arithmetic (or a unit test of it) on a fixture state where the only `not_met` criterion is evidence-only: no debug gap is produced for it and the decision is to exit, not to debug; saved under `evidence/FS-10/`

criteria.statement: A run whose only failures are `not_met` rulings on `evidence-only` criteria exits `satisfied`, under the default blocking policy as well as under `Blocking: must-pass only`
criteria.cites: After s4: "never fails a run on one"; Today s2: "Under the default blocking policy a `not_met` on any frame ... blocks `satisfied`" (the behaviour this replaces)
criteria.evidence: Loop outcome computed (or unit-tested) for that fixture state under each blocking policy, both reading `satisfied`; saved under `evidence/FS-11/`

criteria.statement: `evidence-only` criteria are left out of the coverage ratio, so unproven evidence-only rows cannot push a run below the coverage floor
criteria.cites: domain-derived: the source says the loop "never fails a run on one" (After s4); a run whose coverage falls below the floor exits `insufficient-coverage`, so counting an unproven evidence-only row in the ratio would let it fail the run, which the source rules out
criteria.evidence: Coverage figure computed (or unit-tested) for a fixture with N `core` rows all `met` and several `evidence-only` rows `not_met`: the ratio counts only the `core` rows and the run does not exit `insufficient-coverage`; saved under `evidence/FS-12/`

criteria.statement: An `evidence-only` frame is still captured and shown for review: its row appears in the verification report with its screenshot, even though its ruling cannot fail the run
criteria.cites: domain-derived: the source keeps a generated row for every non-default frame (After s3) and records it in the success definition (After s4) rather than dropping it, and names its class "evidence-only"; a row that kept its place but captured nothing would provide no evidence, so the frame is still exercised and reported
criteria.evidence: A verification report rendered from a fixture run in which an evidence-only row carries a screenshot, showing that row with its image (an ``/image link naming the capture); saved under `evidence/FS-13/`

criteria.statement: A `core` design-comparison criterion is must-pass: under the default blocking policy (`Blocking: all`) a `not_met` ruling on it stops the run from exiting `satisfied`
criteria.cites: After s4: "a `core` row is must-pass"; Today s2: "Under the default blocking policy a `not_met` on any frame ... blocks `satisfied`"
criteria.evidence: Loop outcome computed (or unit-tested) for a fixture state with one `core` row `not_met`, under the default policy: outcome is not `satisfied`; saved under `evidence/FS-14/`

criteria.statement: A `core` design-comparison criterion still blocks under `Blocking: must-pass only`: a `not_met` ruling on it stops the run from exiting `satisfied` and is not filed as a non-blocking defect
criteria.cites: After s4: "a `core` row is must-pass"; Today s3: "under `Blocking: must-pass only` none of them block" (the behaviour this replaces)
criteria.evidence: Loop outcome computed (or unit-tested) for the same fixture state under `Blocking: must-pass only`: outcome is not `satisfied` and the `core` row is not in the non-blocking list; saved under `evidence/FS-15/`

criteria.statement: Each of the 3 design commands, `/create-design`, `/refine-design` and `/audit-design`, carries the Core rule: at most 8 Core boards, and only `to-be` and `as-is` boards may be Core
criteria.cites: After s5: "`/create-design`, `/refine-design` and `/audit-design` carry the Core rule"; After s1 for the rule's content: "at most 8 are Core, and only `to-be` and `as-is` boards may be"
criteria.evidence: `grep` output over each of the 3 command prompt files showing the Core rule stated in each; saved under `evidence/FS-16/`

criteria.statement: A lib step writes the Core marker into the `canvas.json` title of each Core board, and leaves the title of every non-Core board unmarked
criteria.cites: After s5: "a lib step writes the Core marker into each Core board's `canvas.json` title"; that non-Core titles stay unmarked is domain-derived: a marker placed on every board would distinguish nothing
criteria.evidence: The lib step run on a fixture design's `canvas.json`, with the file before and after (or a `diff`), showing the marker in each Core board's title and in no other; saved under `evidence/FS-17/`
